2609.01257.title: Measuring the Behavioral Fidelity of Long-Horizon Human Activity Simulations
2609.01257.paper_summary: As LLM-based human simulators are increasingly used for policy, evaluation, and training, they must faithfully reproduce real behavioral patterns. While prior work has examined behavioral fidelity in survey responses and dialogue, longer-horizon real-world activity remains largely unexplored. We introduce a framework for evaluating behavioral fidelity in long-horizon activity simulations across temporal granularities and levels of analysis. As a case study, we collect a 43-hour multi-camera dataset of in-the-wild office activity and compare trace-derived conditioning mechanisms: persona descriptors, few-shot exemplars, and statistical transition and time-of-day priors. We find that behavioral fidelity is not uniform across metrics: statistical priors bring activity and sequence distributions closest to real behavior, yet over-fragment routines and suppress within-person variability. These findings motivate a more holistic evaluation that spans multiple metrics, temporal granularities, and levels of analysis.
2609.01257.paper_summary_zh: 隨著基於LLM的人類模擬器在政策、評估和訓練中的使用日益增加，它們必須忠實地再現真實的行為模式。雖然之前的研究已經檢視了調查回應和對話中的行為忠實度，但長期現實活動仍然在很大程度上未被探索。我們介紹了一個框架，用於評估長期活動模擬中的行為忠實度，涵蓋不同的時間粒度和分析層級。作為案例研究，我們收集了一個43小時的多攝影機野外辦公活動數據集，並比較了基於痕跡的條件機制：角色描述符、少量示例和統計轉移及時間先驗。我們發現行為忠實度在各指標間並不均勻：統計先驗使活動和序列分佈最接近真實行為，但卻過度碎片化常規並抑制個體內變異性。這些發現促使我們進行更全面的評估，涵蓋多個指標、時間粒度和分析層級。
